newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power softer on seasonal temps.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power softer on seasonal temps.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity values in the northeastern U.S. Wednesday ended softer than Tuesday's levels as seasonal weather continued in the region.
"I don't see cold weather coming our way. I don't see anything abnormal," said a New York trader.
For Thursday, temperatures in the Northeast were again expected to peak in 30s-40s Fahrenheit and bottom in the 20s-30s.
Moderate power demand mitigated growing concerns over surging prices of natural gas and fuel oil for electric generation in December.

December prices of natgas delivered to utility receipt points in the New York City area were notationally assessed at $4.75 per million British thermal units, reflecting soaring values in other parts of the U.S. amid high spot demand and winter storage concerns.
New York City gate swing natural gas prices today rose to $4.00 per million British thermal units, sharply higher than Tuesday's $3.50.

The rally in domestic and Canadian natgas prices also spurred fuel oil values. The widely used one-percent sulphur grade in the New York harbor was last pegged at $21.50-$21.75 a barrel or $3.41-$3.45 per mmBtu.
Today, Hydro-Quebec resumed normal service on one of the two export power line to New York state.
The Canadian utility on Tuesday halved the typical 800 megawatts (MW) of energy to the New York Power Authority. It was repairing a transformer along the high-voltage line.
In the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) district, peak, non-firm electricity for Thursday was again quoted at $22.00-$24.00 a megawatt hour (MWh).
Western NYPP power for non-firm delivery during light load hours on Thursday remained steady $14.00.
In the eastern part of NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for Thursday was assessed at $26.00-$28.00, lower than Tuesday's range of $28.00-$29.00.
Off-peak, non-firm Thursday electricity in eastern NYPP held again at $17.00-$18.00.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Thursday at the Northeast Utilities border was assessed at $30.00-$31.00, down from Tuesday's $33.00-$34.00.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Thursday delivery to the NU border was pegged near $21.00, compared with Tuesday's offers at $23.00-$24.00.
The 619 megawatt (MW) oil-fired Wyman 4 generating unit in Yarmouth, Maine, as expected, resumed full output Tuesday after being shut October 5 for seasonal maintenance.
